title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 0-RTT Replay Protection Architecture
purpose: Define DNS opcode classification for replayability, client-side 0-RTT gating, and server-side 0-RTT transaction handling with queue limits.
design_summary: Three independent layers: (1) DoqDefaults.IsReplayableOpcode classifies DNS opcodes 0 (QUERY) and 4 (NOTIFY) as replayable and all others as non-replayable. (2) DoqClient exposes AllowZeroRtt; when enabled, QueryAsync rejects non-replayable opcodes with a clear exception. (3) DoqServer and DoqServerOptions add MaxQueuedZeroRttTransactions to limit queued 0-RTT queries; DoqQueryContext carries an IsZeroRtt signal (default false, not yet wired to transport). Non-replayable 0-RTT transactions receive a REFUSED response with Extended DNS Error "Too Early".
data_and_state_considerations: The server gains a queue of pending 0-RTT transactions bounded by MaxQueuedZeroRttTransactions. The client adds a boolean AllowZeroRtt flag.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The transport layer does not currently expose 0-RTT detection on the server side; DoqQueryContext.IsZeroRtt defaults to false and is a placeholder for future transport integration.
OPCODE values beyond the registered range are treated as non-replayable.
REFUSED response with EDE Too Early (option code 20) is constructed inline.
risks: The 0-RTT detection abstraction point (IsZeroRtt on DoqQueryContext) is not wired to the transport until the QUIC layer exposes early data state.

supplemental_sections.heading: Transport Limitation
supplemental_sections.content: The repository's QuicConnection.ConnectAsync public entry point does not expose 0-RTT state. The DoqServer.HandleConnectionAsync cannot currently detect whether an inbound stream arrived in 0-RTT data. A future slice may wire the IsZeroRtt flag when the transport API is extended.
